description: Tell Skein about things Claude Code otherwise never reports on its own. SessionStart (#273): a freshly spawned harness can leave the "spawning" activity phase even before a first prompt writes anything to its transcript. It carries no matcher on purpose, so it fires for every `source` (`startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, `fork`) rather than only the first — a repeat or phantom fire is harmless because the frontend handler is idempotent, recording a timestamp and only moving the phase when the transcript tail hasn't already spoken for itself, never overriding a permission dialog or an exited harness. A second, synchronous SessionStart entry (#318) only acts when Skein loaded this plugin through CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS (a `claude` typed into a harness's post-exit shell): it appends an `unset` to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, which Claude Code sources before each Bash-tool command, so a nested `claude -p` started through the Bash tool does not load Skein's plugin too (it does NOT cover the PowerShell tool). SessionEnd (#318): in a post-exit shell Skein binds the pane to the first claude that starts there and releases it when that claude's session ends. PermissionRequest (#86): Claude Code is blocked on a permission dialog, so the room can show "permission required" as its own activity phase instead of folding it into end-of-turn waiting. The env-file `unset` of CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS also removes, from Bash-tool children, a value the user set themselves; that is an accepted cost of keeping nested claude children off Skein's hooks.
